Where it began

Bhuvneshwar Kumar was born in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, on 5 February 1990. He was thirteen when he first went to a proper coaching centre, and by 17 he was making his first-class debut for Uttar Pradesh, against Bengal.

He soon gave notice of what was coming. In the Ranji Trophy final of 2008–09 he dismissed Sachin Tendulkar for nought, and no bowler had ever done that to him in first-class cricket before. It is the sort of first that a young man from Meerut could happily dine out on for years.

The player

He arrived in international cricket at the end of 2012 against Pakistan, taking a wicket in his first over on his Twenty20 international debut and then one with his very first ball in one-day internationals. His Test debut followed in 2013, the year he helped India win the Champions Trophy and was picked in the ICC's team of the tournament.

In 21 Tests between 2013 and 2018 he took 63 wickets at 26.10, with four five-wicket innings. The finest came at Lord's in 2014, when he took 6 for 82 and was named India's player of the series in England. He could hold a bat too: 552 Test runs, with three fifties and a best of 63 not out.

What made him special

Swing was his gift. A bowler of medium pace rather than raw speed, he could move the ball both ways almost at will, and that was enough to trouble the best. No Indian before him had taken five wickets in an innings in all three international formats, and his first wicket in each of the three formats was bowled, which suggests he liked to aim at the stumps.

Test cricket saw rather less of him than his record deserved. Twenty-one Tests feels a small number for a bowler with his touch, but they were good ones.

Away from the middle

The Indian Premier League brought him plenty of success. In 2016 he took 23 wickets for Sunrisers Hyderabad as they won the title, and he was the first bowler to win the Purple Cap, for the season's most wickets, in two seasons running. He won the competition again with Royal Challengers Bengaluru in 2025. He was named the ICC's Player of the Month for March 2021, and was the leading wicket-taker at the 2022 Asia Cup with 11. In October 2026 he was called back into India's Twenty20 squad for a series against New Zealand.

And finally

In July 2013, in a three-nation tournament, he took four wickets for eight runs against Sri Lanka, finished with more wickets than anyone and was named player of the series. Two runs for each wicket is roughly what it felt like to face him on a morning when the ball was swinging.
